items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: We played at the Follies Theater over there in Brooklyn with Ralph Cooper and his review.

ctx.x: Yes, different places. Did you travel much?

Well, we traveled every night for almost ten years. We covered 38 states. We covered most every city in every state. You take the state of Texas, which is the largest state in the United States. We covered four corners of Texas. It's not a city in the state that we even far west Texas, a little bit of towns like Pampa. We played those towns, Odessa, before they were ever brought up to in population like they are now. We didn't miss any towns. In Louisiana, we found backwards that we didn't even know existed in…
What year would this be then, Don?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: He was just like Larry Steele and those guys who don't know anything about him. I only heard their name.

ctx.x: Well, I guess sometimes you'd get top billing and sometimes you wouldn't. Well, yeah. It was very.

Top billing and most of the time in the cities but on the stages might have been a review. So, you're just another part of the review. So, for instance, this is Ralph Cooper's review. Mm-hmm. Featuring Don Albert's Big Bang. Who was Ralph Cooper? Ralph Cooper was a producer in New York. Mm-hmm. He was just like Larry Steele and those guys who don't know anything about him. I only heard their name. But they were producers. He produced the show at the Fowlers in Brooklyn. That's where Ella and all these other…
Yeah, well, that's more honest than the way they do things now sometimes. I don't know.
